cultural.vision_reason: The cloth shows classic Asante kente strip weaving (multicoloured woven strips) alternating with adinkra-stamped panels bearing recognizable adinkrahene and other stamped symbols, both hallmark Ashanti/Akan textile traditions.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Cloth; made of hand-woven cotton; strips of multicoloured (blue, white, pink, yellow, green and black) "kente" cloth alternating with white cloth (sewn together lengthwise) stamped with two alternating squares of black adinkra stamps: 1) diagonal cross-hatched lines with solid black squares inside, with adinkra stamp showing concentric circles ("adinkrahene" the chief of the adinkra symbols, representing greatness, charisma or leadership) at centre and four corners; 2) repeating adinkra stamp showing flower inside semicircle ("osram ne nsoromma" translated " the moon and the star" representing love, faithfulness and harmony).
